The essentials

Read this firstContents

Everything you need on one screen. The official word on the meet is always the York Train Fair Member Notice (Dealer Notice) and easterntca.com. Last-minute changes are posted on the Calendar of Events posters around the grounds.

RV parking

Free Wi-Fi on the grounds

Pick the network named after the building you are in (the fairgrounds name, not the hall color; see the hall decoder).

Password: yec#2026!!

Public, unsecured network. Avoid banking on it.

Who gets in where

Pre-Show (Purple Hall, Mon to Thu): free and open to everyone.

Public halls (Orange, Purple, Black, Fri and Sat): adults $25 wristband at the Orange Hall lobby. Kids 18 and under free with an adult.

Member halls (Blue, Red, Silver, White): TCA members and registered guests. Guests and the public can see the whole fair, member halls included, one time only for $20 (Silver Hall desk or Orange Hall ticket window).

Badges, maps, help

Registration and badge pickup: Silver Hall. Thu 9-5, Fri 8-5, Sat 9-2.

Wear your badge at all times. Reprints are $5.

Free shuttle between all halls: Fri 9:30-4:30, Sat 9:30-4:00.

Parking is free. Clem calls it the best deal for a 6-day train meet in all the land.

New for October 2026

New

York Train Fair documentary premieres

Caleb Easter's film about York and what it means to the people who make it. Playing all day Thursday in the Verandah Room. You might be in it.

New

Five Verandah Room seminars

Cab 3/Base 3, the future of buying and selling, a social media panel, a manufacturers' panel and a custom-run car presentation. See seminars.

Wednesday Welcome Party

5:30 pm, Verandah Room. $10 covers dinner, dessert and drinks; cash bar available. Tickets: 585-683-9333, some at the door.

Pre-Show selling

Want a Pre-Show table? 8' tables are $50 for all three days. You need a PA Sales Tax License (free online). Checks to EDTCA, mailed to Russell Youens, 110 Slash Drive, Ashland VA 23995. Questions: JRYOUENS@VERIZON.NET

Free coffee and donuts, twice

Friday 7:30 am with the Standard Gauge folks in Black Hall. Saturday 7:30 am in the Orange Hall lobby, courtesy of the Eastern Division.

Last call at the Lyndon Diner

The Lyndon Diner on Route 30 closes for good in early 2027. Enjoy it while you can this October.

Services

Food

  • Orange Hall: large food service inside (burgers, hot dogs, fish, fries, nachos); food trucks outside (pizza, crab cakes, funnel cakes, lemonade)
  • Blue Hall: sit-down service at the back
  • Between Blue & Silver: hot dog counter with seating
  • Blue/Silver parking lot: BBQ, chicken strips, fries, funnel cakes
  • Between Red & White: burgers, funnel cakes, lemonade
  • Pre-Show (Mon-Thu): food truck outside Purple Hall

Restrooms & water

  • Inside Blue, White and Black Halls
  • Lobby between Blue and Silver (water fountains here)
  • Outside Red Hall, east side, by First Aid
  • Both sides of the Orange Hall Promenade (water fountains here)
  • Open 24/7: west side of Orange Hall Promenade (outside entrance, coin showers: $0.50 for 4 min) and the First Aid building

Clem's rule: never pass a water fountain. Steam engines and humans both need water.

Money

Four ATMs: two inside Orange Hall, one in the Blue Hall lobby, one outside Red Hall (toward White Hall).

Orange and Purple table holders need a PA Sales Tax number. State staff do visit, so have your license handy.

Health & mobility

First Aid: next to the Fire Station.

Scooters & wheelchairs: American Scooter Rentals, next to First Aid. No reservation needed.

Clem says: prep your meds, put them where you can find them, and take them.

Shipping

UPS will wrap and ship your finds. Lobby between Blue and Silver Halls. Fri 9-4, Sat 9-2.

Lost, found or stolen

Turn in found items and file lost-item reports at the Silver Hall registration desk. Coordinator Bob Heine, 301-585-1280, Robert.j.heine@gmail.com.

TCA National

The National Business Office has staffed tables in the Orange Hall lobby: membership help, applications, merchandise. Museum and Library deaccession tables are in Orange Hall, and every purchase supports them.

Visitor info

Explore York has guides, brochures and PA maps in Silver and Orange Halls. yorkpa.org

Getting here

Directions & trafficContents

From the south (Baltimore)

Take the Baltimore Beltway (I-695) to I-83 North into Pennsylvania. Exit right onto George St (83 Business). Left on Country Club Rd, past York College. Right on S Richland Ave, left at the light onto W Market St, then right into the fairgrounds. You enter by Blue Hall.

From the north

Take I-83 South to Route 30 West. Follow Route 30 to Route 74. Turn right onto N Highland Ave, then left into the fairgrounds. You enter by Orange Hall.

Clem's traffic tip: the Carlisle Ave gate can be horrendous. Use Gate 6 on Highland Avenue at the northwest end (go past Orange Hall to the fence). It is always open and you can turn left or right easily.

Traffic radio

  • WSBA AM 910
  • WSOX FM 96.1
  • WROZ FM 101.1 "The Rose"
  • WGAL Channel 8 TV, every 10 min, 5-7 am

Rules, registration & guests

The fine print, made readableContents

Four ways to register

  1. Online at yorkregistration.org
  2. Call the Eastern Division Call Center, 585-683-9333
  3. By mail, using the form in the Meet Notice
  4. In person at the Silver Hall desk

While you're here, pre-register for April 2027.

Bringing a guest

  • A guest is anyone over 18 who isn't a TCA member or applicant.
  • Members can host as many guests as they like, registered in advance.
  • Guests pick up their badge in person with a photo ID. Guest badges are not mailed.
  • A guest can attend York once. After that, join TCA (you can join on the spot).

Show rules

  • Registering means you agree to Eastern Division and TCA rules.
  • Keep your badge visible at all times, and never let anyone else wear it.
  • Every item on your table must be priced.
  • Altered items need a TCA "Identatag" (Registration Desk or a hall captain).
  • Sellers of reproduction parts must display a Certificate of Compliance.
  • No buying, selling or trading during setup. Only empty boxes may leave the hall during setup.
  • Still photography is fine in all halls, but not of copyrighted material. Not sure? Ask.
  • Cell phones are fine; step outside for calls.
  • Follow the yellow arrows on hall floors.
  • No handcarts, dollies, suitcases or large backpacks in the halls.
  • Single-width strollers are fine.
  • No smoking, no vehicles in the halls, no alcohol on the grounds.
  • Private golf carts need a $1 million liability certificate on file with the fairgrounds.
  • Only licensed service or medical animals inside. Pets are fine on the grounds; clean up after them.
  • Sleeping on the grounds requires the $50 RV fee.

Quick answers

Why didn't I get a Meet Notice?

Usually one of three reasons: you didn't register for a meet in the past year, you joined TCA recently, or the post office lost it. Download the member notice. Still stuck? Contact the Eastern Division.

Where should I stay?

The York County Visitors Bureau lists hotels. RVers, see RV & camping.

Can I help out?

Yes, and volunteers get free admission plus a free Thursday lunch. Needs: hall setup, registration (busiest Fri and Sat), the Orange Hall ticket booth, RV parking (80-100 units), parking signage, Pre-Show setup and Kids Korner. Contact Ben Swann, bswannrr@yahoo.com, 804-677-8545. Kids Korner also welcomes donated train items, especially complete sets.

Road trips from the Pittsburgh Independent Hi-Railers

Curated by Andy Hummel (TCA 08-6230) after mornings at the Pre-Show. Read Andy's full list.

The York Week Wednesday Grand Tour

About 45 minutes of driving for the first three stops, then an hour to Red Lion. Arrive early and explore the town over dinner.

  1. White Rose Hobbies, 4401 W Market St, York. Lots of hobby supplies. site
  2. Toy Trains Unlimited open house, 38 York St, Hanover
  3. Iron Horse Trains inside Yesteryear Antique Center, 441 Pine St, Hanover. Good in-store stock, plus antique dealers with layout-ready finds. site
  4. Red Lion Train Station open house, 73 N Main St, Red Lion

Strasburg (1 hour)

Too much for one day. Pick a few.

  1. TCA National Toy Train Museum, 300 Paradise Ln, Ronks
  2. Choo Choo Barn and Strasburg Train Shop, 226 Gap Rd. The shop carries almost the entire Arttista figure line.
  3. Strasburg Rail Road, 301 Gap Rd, Ronks
  4. Railroad Museum of Pennsylvania, 300 Gap Rd
  5. Barry's Car Barn, 3504 Old Philadelphia Pike, Intercourse (15 min away). Classic cars, motorcycles and vintage train sets. Closed Sun and Mon.
  6. On Wednesday, stop at the Lower Susquehanna Valley open house in Columbia on the way back.

Gettysburg (1 hour)

  1. Carver's Toy Trains, 305 Buford Ave. Small outside, packed inside, mostly O gauge. Mon-Sat 9-5, Sun 10:30-5. 717-334-6937
  2. Tommy Gilbert's Hobby Shop, 346 E Water St. Modeling supplies and books. Closed Tuesdays.
  3. Lincoln Train Museum, 425 Steinwehr Ave. Very short hours, so plan ahead.

Baltimore and Mt. Airy (1.5 hours)

  1. B&O Railroad Museum, 901 W Pratt St, Baltimore. 10-4.
  2. The Toy Exchange, 1001 Twin Arch Rd #12, Mt. Airy, MD (40 min on). Trains and famous vintage toys. Mon-Sat 10-7, Sun noon-5.
  3. Dinner at Twin Arch Tavern, a few doors down.

Stories

From the people who make YorkContents

Welcome to York

Bob Buehler, Eastern Division President · buehlster@aol.com

On behalf of the Eastern Division, it is my pleasure to welcome you to another York Train Fair. Whether this is your first visit or you have been attending for decades, I hope you enjoy everything that makes York such a special tradition: the trains, the discoveries, and, most importantly, the friendships renewed throughout the halls.

As I prepare to conclude my time serving as President of the Eastern Division, this York carries special meaning for me. It has been a tremendous honor and privilege to serve our membership. I am deeply grateful for the confidence you placed in me and for the encouragement and friendship you have shown throughout my tenure.

The Eastern Division's success is made possible by the officers, directors, committee members, volunteers, and countless others who contribute their time and talents. York simply could not happen without their dedication. I extend my sincere thanks to every person who has worked behind the scenes to support the Division and make this meet possible.

Although my time as President is coming to an end, my commitment to the Eastern Division and the York tradition will continue. I look forward to remaining involved, supporting our future leadership, and sharing many more York memories with all of you.

Thank you for giving me the privilege of serving as your President. Please enjoy the show, support our vendors, welcome our guests, and take time to appreciate the fellowship that has made York such an important part of our hobby for generations. Welcome to York and thank you for being part of the Eastern Division family.

Clem's (and Ryan's) Report

A day-by-day look back at Spring York, April 2026, by Ryan Newman

Sunday. We arrived Sunday afternoon and unloaded into the Purple Hall for the Pre-Show. As has become tradition, the wind was raging and keeping things very cool. A great turnout of vendors: 1932 Blue 400TW tenders with original boxes, and probably the most Ives tenders ever for sale in one place. Marty V stopped by as we set up. Dinner at the Lyndon Diner on Route 30. I had the French toast.

Monday. The Pre-Show opened at 7:30 am so vendors could finish setting up. Donuts were plentiful, though from Walmart, on a rumor that maple donuts might not arrive in time. Good crowd, as usual on Mondays. Katie and Rupert were across from us in their usual spot. Lots of nice McCoy cars, and a homemade standard gauge switcher built from what looks like an 8 shell. Good sales day, and I acquired a few more trains myself. Dinner at Rivertowne Bar and Grill in Wrightsville; Robert and I split a large supreme pizza.

Tuesday. Breakfast and lunch sandwiches from the Rutter's in Abbottstown, where the ladies check the Eastern Division website to know when we're in town. One of them had asked about a train set on the cheap, and she and her husband are now proud owners of a 2026 with a 2466WX tender, three freight cars, a 6457 lighted caboose, track and a transformer. Robert handed out serendipitous gifts to fellow sellers (Katie got a music box match box). We closed the night at the Welcome Party in its new home, the Verandah Room: quieter, nicer, and you can actually talk. BBQ chicken, spareribs, baked potato, macaroni salad, tossed salad and three kinds of cobbler.

Wednesday. Another Pre-Show complete. I sold lots of "Majestic" items and picked up some very nice ones. A Märklin One Gauge brass tunnel and a large One Gauge live steamer appeared in the Purple Hall, which the OGR Forum called "Majestic." The volunteer lunch had a great turnout, and Kids Korner setup began as Mighty Casey returned. Dinner at Graybill's Route 30 Diner: the Salisbury steak special. It was Majestic.

Thursday. Members moved into their halls. I heard a loud rumble outside, wandered to the Black Hall, and met Rupert Campbell coming out. "Yeah! STOMPER arrived!" There sat STOMPER on the SGMA layout, apparently powered to the fairgrounds by gravity waves. Decent crowd, closed at 6. Wing night at the New Era in Abbottstown.

Friday. My plan was the SGMA show and tell and, finally, a maple donut. But at 7:25 am fair maintenance was waiting for me to unlock the Purple Hall. Duty calls. By the time I was free, the donuts were gone. Good sales day anyway. Purple Hall had the best pricing on McCoy convention cars. I bought an original-paint 752W set, felt unsure about the price, then found a boxed one in Silver Hall with better paint, worse frames, likely swapped vestibules, at 1.5 times what I paid. Boxes are nice, but you can't run the boxes. That night we visited the Lower Susquehanna club's Run What You Brung; they've almost doubled their layout since October.

A word from Clem himself

Guys and gals, Saturday is not the end of all. It is the beginning of all. Think of what has happened to you and yours, kids and friends. You got lots of new friends and lots of new stories right here. When you're playing golf at the 13th hole you can say, let me tell you about what this guy paid for this stupid engine. Collect the business cards you picked up and get them in your address book, because you're going to want to call Louie, who offered you a Blue Comet for 40 bucks. Take notes on where you ate dinner, so next year you know where you were.

Please think about how amazing this is. There are people, registration and financial folks, who work so the rest of us can play trains and have fun. Don't forget it. God bless those folks serving under the Red, White and Blue. I'll see you guys this fall. Good night, everybody. Clem

Friday night, the part I forgot. The Ice Cream Social included a special presentation. Last year the Eastern Division created an award for members who have made an impact on the division and exemplify the purpose of TCA. It is named for its first recipient, Richard "Clem" Clement. The second Richard "Clem" Clement Award went to Hope Danielson.

Saturday. I finally got my maple donut. During coffee and donuts, longtime York attendee and TCA member Eddie Goldman was remembered; his daughter Lisa was there. And to anyone who says York isn't what it used to be: Kids Korner had over 80 kids on Saturday alone, and stayed open until 1 pm instead of noon because it couldn't close. I spent the day walking the grounds with my nephew, introducing him to friends in every hall. Just before the member halls closed, a steady rain began, as if Mother Nature were sad that York was ending for six months.

As Clem wrote, whatever comes next, we keep the memories and friends from this York and all the ones before it.

About the Primer

Clem's Primer began many years ago as the personal experiences and views of Richard "Clem" Clement: TCA Past President, Eastern Division Past President, past TCA Director, past WB&A Chapter Vice President and board member, and most importantly a TCA member in good standing. Carol R. McGinnis, TCA Past President and Heritage Member, authored it through April 2024. It is now edited by Eastern Division member Ryan Newman, with information gathered from many sources.

The Primer is meant to enrich your York experience. It is not sponsored by any organization and does not endorse any product. The Eastern Division York Train Show Notice is the official newsletter. This edition replaces all previous versions. Past editions.

Our namesake

Richard "Clem" ClementContents

Clem Clement, TCA Honor Roll #64-987, is the namesake of this well-read and well-distributed TCA publication. He and his wife Sandy continue to add their expertise, wit, and by default his name to this publication. His knowledge and experiences add to the details and to the fun. Just ask him!

He loves to ask the "hard" questions, bring up history and mention members by name, and he challenges each of us to increase our love and knowledge of trains and to increase TCA membership.

Thanks, Clem!
